$description: avenCEO brand tokens. THE source of truth: the TypeScript package loads this file and adds types, it does not hold values. DTCG shape ($type/$value); values may reference other tokens with var(--color-...) exactly as the emitted CSS does.
name: avenCEO

tones.$description: The brand identity. Four hues, and nothing that only carries a meaning — a colour in here is one the logo and the marketing may use. Sorted by hue.

marine.$description: the brand blue. Also the ground the dark theme stands on.

paradise.$description: the deeper blue-teal — work in motion.

sunflower.$description: the highlight. Sunflower, not "gold" — the generic word loses the name.

palettes.$description: Ordered colour sets a generator walks. Not roles — nothing here is picked by meaning, only by index — so they live apart from the role map.

avatar.$description: The five colours a generated identicon draws from, light to dark. They are the logo's own palette and used to sit in the website as a bare array, which meant a second brand could not have its own and a change here reached nothing.

functional.$description: Colours that carry a MEANING and are never identity. Neither appears in the logo, and neither may be used as a brand accent — reaching for the failure tone to decorate something is the mistake this separation exists to prevent.

terracotta.$description: the failure pigment. Kept its own name: a TONE is named for the paint and a ROLE for the meaning, so `terracotta` and `error` are different words for a reason. It lives here rather than in `tones` because it is never identity — it appears in no logo and must not decorate.

surfaces.$description: Every surface a page stands on, in both themes. The LIGHT ladder is the sand family (the brand cream); the DARK ladder is the marine family. Named `<theme>-<rung>`, so a theme is a prefix and adding dark is adding rows. The dark ladder is declared and NOT yet wired — nothing renders from it until a theme selects it.

light-page.$description: the page itself — the lightest sand.

light-selected.$description: a card the user has chosen — sand at full strength.

dark-page.$description: the page itself — marine, one step below the brand tone.

dark-raised.$description: lifted off the page — the brand marine.

dark-selected.$description: a card the user has chosen.

ink.$description: Text guaranteed to read on a filled colour. Concrete values, not derivations: these used to be `color-mix(... N%, black)` computed at render time in seven places, which meant the system could not tell you what colour its own text was without a browser. Same rendered values, now nameable and checkable.

on-light.$description: on any light rung — the brand marine.

white.$description: true white. Named because the system uses it in exactly two places.

on-primary-soft.$description: the de-emphasised step of text on a primary fill. 9.44:1. Replaces `text-primary-foreground/80`, which said the same thing as a relationship to whatever was behind it — and a relationship inverts between themes while a named colour does not.

on-primary-quiet.$description: the quiet step of text on a primary fill — footer meta, legal line. 6.78:1.

on-dark-soft.$description: the lead line over media: on-dark at 94%.

on-dark-quiet.$description: the helper line over media: on-dark at 72%.

roles.$description: What the paint MEANS. ONE group: the site/app split it replaced held six tokens that aliased shared roles under different names and one that differed, which is not a vocabulary, it is a synonym list. A surface that does not use `evidence` simply does not use it. A role prefixed `dark-` is that role's value under `[data-theme="dark"]`: the generator strips the prefix and emits it in the dark block, the same derivation the surfaces use. Only roles that actually differ need one. The `border-strong`/`border-soft`/`track`/`error-surface`/`error-border` roles exist because those values used to be alphas of another colour, which cannot be themed: an alpha carries a RELATIONSHIP to whatever is behind it, and that relationship inverts between a pale ground and a dark one.

foreground-soft.$description: body copy, held back one step — a lede under a heading, a supporting paragraph. 6.30:1 on the darkest light surface. This is the middle of THREE named emphasis steps (foreground, foreground-soft, foreground-quiet); the site used to spell it `text-foreground/80`.

muted.$description: a quiet fill. Was a color-mix of marine into the page.

muted-foreground.$description: quiet copy. WARNING: 3.66:1 on the page ground — this FAILS AA as text and must not be used for any. `foreground-quiet` is the readable step. Kept for non-text uses pending its own fix.

primary-edge.$description: The rim of a primary button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see — at 22% the two were the same colour at arm's length, which is a border that costs a declaration and reads as nothing. 2.93:1 against the fill.

primary-ring.$description: The halo a primary button grows on hover and while loading. The fill, softened into the page, so it reads as the button's own light rather than as a second border.

primary-foreground-soft.$description: text on primary, held back one step.

primary-foreground-quiet.$description: the quiet step of text on primary — footer meta, the legal line.

secondary.$description: THE SECOND BRAND COLOUR. Paradise. Stated once here so every role that means "the second colour" points at this rather than naming the tone — `progress` did, `band` did, and the three had no way of moving together. It replaces a `secondary` that pointed at a sand SURFACE, which was a surface wearing an action name.

secondary-foreground.$description: text on the second brand colour.

tertiary.$description: THE THIRD BRAND COLOUR. Turquoise. Same rule: `success` and `band-alt` both meant this and both named the tone.

tertiary-foreground.$description: text on the third brand colour.

band.$description: A full-bleed editorial band in a brand tone. Darkened from the tone by ~5% so WHITE clears 4.5:1 on it — paradise itself gives 3.89:1 and 3.12:1, which is to say neither white nor dark text reads on the raw tone at body size. There is no soft or quiet step on a band: at this contrast there is no room for one, and de-emphasising with a paler grey on a saturated colour is weak typography anyway. Hierarchy on a band comes from size and weight.

band-alt.$description: the second editorial band, from the THIRD brand colour. Same rule, same 4.6:1 with white.

band-foreground.$description: the only text colour a band carries.

scrim-thin.$description: The glass bar: the page ground at 90%, so the content behind reads through the blur without the text on top losing its ground. Named, because this lived as an inline `color-mix(surface-page 10%, transparent)` in a `style` attribute in one component — unthemeable, and 10% is far too thin to sit text on.

scrim.$description: The veil over hero media. 32% marine — enough that the light ink reads on any frame the video lands on, little enough that the scene is still a scene. It was three stacked `color-mix` stops in one component.

scrim-strong.$description: 50% marine, for the top of a hero where the nav sits.

scrim-heavy.$description: 55% marine, for the bottom of a hero where the copy ends and the next section begins.

scrim-text.$description: The halo under hero text. Not decoration — over a photograph the scrim alone cannot promise contrast on every frame, and this is the second half of that guarantee.

progress.$description: in motion. Points at the RANK rather than at paradise, so the second brand colour and everything that means it move together.

progress-surface.$description: the quiet form of progress — a tint to sit progress-ink on. Concrete, not `bg-progress/15`: an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast, and the site had five different alphas doing this by eye. progress-ink measures 6.66:1 on it.

progress-border.$description: the edge of a progress tint. Decorative — it separates the tint from the page, and the meaning is carried by the ink and the words, never by this line alone.

dark-progress-border.$description: the progress tint edge on dark.

success.$description: settled. Points at the rank rather than at turquoise.

success-edge.$description: The rim of a success button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see — at 22% the two were the same colour at arm's length, which is a border that costs a declaration and reads as nothing. 1.56:1 against the fill.

success-ring.$description: The halo a success button grows on hover and while loading. The fill, softened into the page, so it reads as the button's own light rather than as a second border.

success-surface.$description: the quiet form of success — a tint to sit success-ink on. Concrete, not `bg-success/15`: an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast, and the site had five different alphas doing this by eye. success-ink measures 6.44:1 on it.

success-border.$description: the edge of a success tint. Decorative — it separates the tint from the page, and the meaning is carried by the ink and the words, never by this line alone.

dark-success-border.$description: the success tint edge on dark.

warning-surface.$description: the quiet form of warning — a tint to sit warning-ink on. Concrete, not `bg-warning/15`: an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast, and the site had five different alphas doing this by eye. warning-ink measures 5.20:1 on it.

warning-border.$description: the edge of a warning tint. Decorative — it separates the tint from the page, and the meaning is carried by the ink and the words, never by this line alone.

dark-warning-border.$description: the warning tint edge on dark.

error-edge.$description: The rim of a error button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see — at 22% the two were the same colour at arm's length, which is a border that costs a declaration and reads as nothing. 1.71:1 against the fill.

error-ring.$description: The halo a error button grows on hover and while loading. The fill, softened into the page, so it reads as the button's own light rather than as a second border.

info-surface.$description: the quiet form of info — a tint to sit info-ink on. Concrete, not `bg-info/15`: an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast, and the site had five different alphas doing this by eye. info-ink measures 4.48:1 on it.

info-border.$description: the edge of a info tint. Decorative — it separates the tint from the page, and the meaning is carried by the ink and the words, never by this line alone.

dark-info-border.$description: the info tint edge on dark.

accent.$description: the marketing highlight. Same paint as `warning`, different job — and the job is the reason the name survives the merge.

accent-edge.$description: The rim of a accent button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see — at 22% the two were the same colour at arm's length, which is a border that costs a declaration and reads as nothing. 1.21:1 against the fill.

accent-ring.$description: The halo a accent button grows on hover and while loading. The fill, softened into the page, so it reads as the button's own light rather than as a second border.

accent-surface.$description: the quiet form of accent — a tint to sit accent-ink on. Concrete, not `bg-accent/15`: an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast, and the site had five different alphas doing this by eye. accent-ink measures 5.20:1 on it.

accent-border.$description: the edge of a accent tint. Decorative — it separates the tint from the page, and the meaning is carried by the ink and the words, never by this line alone.

dark-accent-border.$description: the accent tint edge on dark.

dark-foreground.$description: body copy on a dark ground.

dark-foreground-soft.$description: the soft step on dark. 5.59:1 on dark-selected.

dark-primary.$description: on dark the primary action inverts — a marine button on a marine page is invisible.

dark-quiet-ink.$description: quiet running text, lightened for a dark ground.

border-strong.$description: a deliberate edge — a band divider. Was 25% of the foreground.

border-soft.$description: a hairline. Was 8% of the foreground.

track.$description: the unfilled part of a rail. Was 12% of the foreground.

error-surface.$description: the wash behind a failure message. Was 8% of terracotta.

error-border.$description: the edge of a failure message. Was 35% of terracotta.

dark-error-surface.$description: the wash behind a failure message on dark.

dark-error-border.$description: the edge of a failure message on dark.

foreground-quiet.$description: the quiet step of the body copy — captions, eyebrows, meta. Measured against the DARKEST light surface (light-selected), not against the page: a caption on a selected card is the same caption, and the old value cleared 4.5 only on the page ground.

dark-foreground-quiet.$description: the quiet step on dark, held to the same rule — it clears 4.5 on dark-selected, the darkest-contrast pairing the dark ladder can produce.

eyebrow-ink.$description: the site eyebrow. Paradise darkened only as far as legibility on the DARKEST ground an eyebrow lands on — which is not the page but a sunflower-tinted panel. Tuning it against the page alone left it at 4.02:1 on light-selected and 4.25:1 on an accent tint.

focus.$description: The focus ring, one colour for the whole estate — sunflower, the brand's own signal colour. DARKENED, and only as far as legibility: raw sunflower #f2ba3d measures 1.44 to 1.71:1 on the light ladder, which is a focus ring nobody can see, and WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the one affordance a keyboard user has. This clears 3.12 to 3.70 on every light surface and still reads as gold.

dark-focus.$description: On dark the brand sunflower needs no darkening — it measures 4.99 to 9.84:1 on the marine ladder, so the ring is the tone itself.

dark-eyebrow-ink.$description: the same eyebrow on a dark ground, where the tone must go LIGHTER rather than darker — which is the whole reason this is a role and not a darkening written at the call site.

secondary-ink.$description: the second brand colour, as running text.

tertiary-ink.$description: the third brand colour, as running text.

secondary-edge.$description: The rim of a secondary button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see.

secondary-ring.$description: The halo a secondary button carries. The fill, softened into the page.

tertiary-edge.$description: The rim of a tertiary button. Lighter than its fill and by enough to see.

tertiary-ring.$description: The halo a tertiary button carries. The fill, softened into the page.

secondary-strong.$description: The second brand colour, darkened until white reads on it — 4.61:1. Raw paradise gives 3.89, so a filled secondary button in the tone itself fails AA at body size. This is the same value the band uses, and for the same reason: a mid-tone cannot carry text without being taken down a step.

tertiary-strong.$description: The third brand colour, darkened until white reads on it — 4.60:1. Raw turquoise gives 3.12.

secondary-surface.$description: the secondary tint, shared with `progress` — same colour, named by rank.

secondary-border.$description: the secondary tint, shared with `progress` — same colour, named by rank.

tertiary-surface.$description: the tertiary tint, shared with `success` — same colour, named by rank.

tertiary-border.$description: the tertiary tint, shared with `success` — same colour, named by rank.

radii.$description: The radius scale, and there is only one. Ten tokens for one idea had accumulated — `chip`, `inner`, `control`, `card`, `panel`, `pill`, plus `lg`, `xl` and `2xl` that duplicated three of them exactly — so the same corner was being chosen by name rather than by size, and two components meaning "a card" could pick different ones. Six steps, roughly Apple's: 6, 10, 14, 20, 28, and full. Every component draws from these and nothing else.

radius-xs.$description: A chip, a tag, an inline pill that is not a button. 6px.

radius-sm.$description: An input, a select, a small control. 10px.

radius-md.$description: A card interior, a well, a nested box. 14px.

radius-xl.$description: A panel, a modal, a sheet. 28px.

radius-full.$description: Buttons, and nothing else. A fully rounded card is a stadium, and a fully rounded input is a pill you cannot tell from a button.

fs-lead.$description: the lead line of a panel

fs-display-lg.$description: the one line above the fold

alpha.$description: One axis, two floors. Both are opacity; the only difference is what it is applied to. Text has a WCAG contrast floor and a surface does not, which is the whole distinction and exactly what the old `ink`/`tint` names hid.

space-hairline.$description: Half a tight. Twelve declarations across the units referenced `--space-hairline` and it was never defined — every one of them computed to nothing, so a `gap` meant for a hair's breadth was zero and the two things it separated touched. Nothing reported it: an undefined custom property is not an error, it is an empty string, and the declaration is simply dropped.

motion.$description:
The motion scale. It did not exist, and 53 declarations across the units referenced it anyway — `--ease-out` 26 times, `--duration-quick` 19, `--duration-moderate` 8. Every one of those transitions was DEAD: an undefined custom property is an empty string, a declaration containing one is discarded whole, and `transition-duration` computed to `0s` on every button in the system. No gate saw it, because a missing transition renders as a working component that simply snaps.

Durations sit inside the 100-300ms band the rules set for UI transitions. `ease-out` for entrances, `ease-in` for exits, `ease-in-out` for a state change that goes and comes back.

duration-instant.$description: A colour swap that should feel immediate but not jump.

duration-quick.$description: The default. Hover, focus, a control changing under the pointer.

duration-moderate.$description: Something ARRIVING — a drawer, a toast, a panel opening.

duration-slow.$description: A whole region changing. Above this the user is waiting for the interface rather than reading it.

ease-out.$description: Entrances. Fast at the start, settling at the end — the thing arrives and stops.

ease-in.$description: Exits. Slow to leave, then gone — nothing decelerates on its way off screen.

ease-in-out.$description: A state change that returns: pressed and released, opened and closed.

z.$description: Stacking order. `--z-overlay` and `--z-sticky` were referenced by the sidebar and the navbar and defined nowhere, so a fixed drawer had no stacking order at all and sat behind the content it was covering. Four steps, far apart, because the point of a scale here is that nobody ever writes `z-index: 9999` to win an argument with a number they cannot see.

z-base.$description: The document. Anything that needs to sit above a sibling and nothing else.

z-sticky.$description: A header or rail that stays while the page scrolls under it.

z-overlay.$description: A drawer, a popover, a dropdown — above the page, below a modal.

z-modal.$description: A dialog and its scrim. Nothing routine goes here.

z-toast.$description: The top. A message about what just happened has to clear a modal, because it may be about the modal.
